bug_semantics: DELETE /api/users/{username} (frigate/api/auth.py delete_user) removed a user by id with no admin-role dependency. GET/POST /users later required require_role(["admin"]), and PUT /users/{username}/password had its own identity check, but delete_user stayed unguarded through v0.16.2. Any authenticated non-admin (viewer) who could hit the route could delete other accounts, including admin, causing integrity loss and DoS. GHSA-vg28-83rp-8xx4 / CVE-2026-33125 (CWE-285) is not withdrawn; GitHub advisory patched versions start at 0.16.3.
flaw_origin: The unguarded delete handler was first written in reconstructed PR #11347 member fafc0aab2fea3ec3eab86fb3a2b02629ca0de497 ("move users to database instead of config", Blake Blackshear). That commit added @AuthBp.route("/users/<username>", methods=["DELETE"]) def delete_user(username): User.delete_by_id(username).execute() with no role check. Parent 7cf3abc850ca3cd335203a5654d801e58a2cc816 has frigate/api/auth.py but only /auth and /login — no users CRUD and no delete_user. Public history later squashed the PR as 1133202cbd12ec6a92fa1b446889ff2d75986def ("Auth! (#11347)"); that squash is not the BIC. FastAPI rewrite cffc431b and viewer-role PR 74ca009 kept the same unguarded DELETE while adding admin deps only on GET/POST /users. Direct fix is 153bcdba3163d5668c7ef927b682a1c592cc0830 ("require admin role to delete users"), landed by squash 592c245dcd25919e7d39bdae2462847c6323850f (PR #21061), first released in v0.16.3.
